# Usage: how this build spends the week's allowance

Written by the lead on 2026-11-22, after the build used a whole week's allowance and three resets in about two days. The founder's words: "this is unacceptable… diagnose and fix this… without compromising any quality", and: "no more fable except you or the top lead, and allow opus to have decision making power". WHERE THIS FILE AND `RUNBOOK.md` DISAGREE, THIS FILE WINS.

## What went wrong (measured, not guessed)

- On the night of 2026-11-17 the lead opened 40 helper sessions in about 70 minutes. Together they cost $551 at list prices, most of them unfinished: a builder's session cost $17 at the middle and up to $32; one audit cost $69; a review on the strongest model cost $8 against $3 on Opus for the same kind of work.
- Nearly nine tenths of that was RE-READING. Every command a session runs makes it read its whole conversation again. Builders had been told to read whole documents (this build's status file alone had grown to 319 KB, the plan to 449 KB), to run the whole gate, to look at dozens of pictures and to wait for GitHub, so a conversation grew to 150,000 to 480,000 tokens and was re-read 500 to 1,100 times: 60 to 200 million tokens for one step.
- Sessions sat waiting (for GitHub, for the lead, for another lane), and a session that waits more than an hour pays full price to read itself again.
- Thirty lanes at once meant thirty half-finished lanes when the allowance ran out, and merges between them.
- An hourly wake-up fired 100 times while nothing could run.
- Reviews turned small things into long fix rounds, and audits added 35 steps in one night.

## The rules

1. **The meter, and the line it must stay under.** HOW TO READ IT (found on 2026-11-22; it takes seconds and costs a third of a cent): the meter speaks when a session starts, so start a tiny one: `create_session` with model `claude-haiku-5-5`, the prompt "Reply with the single word OK and then stop. Do not use any tool.", then, AFTER ONE OTHER COMMAND (the session needs some seconds to start; asked at once it has nothing to say), `list_events` on it with `kinds: ["rate_limit_event"]`: `unifiedWindows.seven_day.utilization` is the share of the week used (0.06 is 6%); then, only once the reading is in hand, `archive_session` (archived too early it never starts). THE LINE (the founder, 2026-11-22: "limit to 20% usage a day (still keep that)", and the aim is the whole plan inside the week's allowance): TWENTY POINTS A DAY, counted from the week's reset: no more than 20% used by the end of the first day (22:00 UTC), 40% by the end of the second, 60%, 80%, and the last 8 points are never spent without the founder in the chat (they are for what the founder finds when they test). Within a day the lead may run ahead of the clock, but never past the day's number. The lead reads the meter at every landing and before opening any lane, and writes it in `STATUS.md`. ABOVE THE LINE: no new helper is started; the ones running finish; what GitHub has passed is landed; `STATUS.md` is brought up to date and pushed; then the lead schedules ONE wake (`send_later`) for a few minutes after the next 22:00 UTC, when the next day's 20 points open, and ends its turn. Three points of the week buy about three helper sessions and their landings. When the founder is in the chat, what they ask comes first, out of the same allowance.
2. **Models.** The strongest model is for the lead only. Builders and reviewers are Opus (effort medium; high only where the lead says so: the scoring screen, sign-in and safety, a migration that changes a guard). Merges, publishing, notes and counting are Sonnet or Haiku.
3. **Three lanes at once, not thirty.** A lane is finished and landed before another is opened. The first test's line first, then the second's, then the rest.
4. **A helper session is short: 80 commands for a builder** (it was 150 until 2026-11-22), 60 for a review, 40 for a confirming look or a small fix. What a session costs grows with the SQUARE of its length, because every command reads again everything the session has seen: measured on 2026-11-22, a builder of 150 commands read 19 to 27 million tokens, one of 65 commands 4 to 7 million. So a big step is cut into parts of about 80 commands, each started fresh from the note the part before it left (`docs/build/handover/lanes/<step>.md`, at most 35 lines), and two parts cost about two thirds of one long session. It never waits: not for GitHub, not for the lead, not for another lane. It writes its note and stops.
5. **Reading.** A helper reads what its brief names and nothing else: never `STATUS.md`, never the whole plan or a whole audit. Long files by search and by line range.
6. **Output.** Every command's output is cut to its last 30 lines (`2>&1 | tail -30`); tests run quietly and are read only where they fail. At most six pictures are looked at in a session.
7. **Checks.** A helper runs `npm run check`, the type check, its own test files and its own browser test. The whole gate runs on GitHub's machines only. The lead reads GitHub's answers for all lanes in one command; a lane lands only on a pass, as before.
8. **Decisions.** A builder decides the technical questions of its step and writes them down (a pending decision file, "Agreed (delegated)"). For a product question it takes the written recommendation, or else the choice that leaves a league's admin the most room and is easiest to change, writes it as a pending decision "Decided for you" with its reason, and builds on. The lead reads every one at landing and may change it. What costs the founder money, needs their hands, touches a live site or real people's data, or goes out in their name still waits for the founder.
9. **Reviews.** One independent review for each lane, on Opus, with a limit. A second one, by use in a browser, only for the scoring screen, for sign-in, and where a child's record is shown. A fix round takes what is High or Medium and inside the step; everything Low is one line in `docs/build/polish.md` and is done in batches. A review's leftover becomes a new step only when it is High.
10. **No new audits** until both tests are in the founder's hands.
11. **`STATUS.md` stays short** (a few screens): now, one line for each lane, what needs the founder. The log is `docs/build/LOG.md`, which nobody is told to read.
12. **Waiting costs nothing, or it is not done.** The lead never asks GitHub by hand in a loop: it starts `node scripts/wait-for-github.mjs <lane> <twin>` as a background command, which wakes it once with the answer. A helper's report wakes the lead. The only timed wake is the one of rule 1, when the lead has stopped for the line. No hourly wake-ups, ever (the one of 2026-11-17 fired 100 times while nothing could run).
13. **The lead's own chat is kept short.** Every command the lead runs reads its whole conversation again, so a lead whose conversation has grown to half a million tokens pays five times as much for each command as one at a hundred thousand. Measured on 2026-11-22: in the two hours before its conversation was shortened the lead cost about as much as the helpers working beside it (a third of everything spent that morning was the lead); in the hour after, a seventh. So: the lead lands a lane with ONE command (`node scripts/land-lane.mjs`; its first lines say how) and not eight by hand, and NEVER while a helper is still working in that lane's folder (the landing removes the folder); it does not read long outputs (every command cut to what is needed, never a whole event or log); it does not read code that a helper can read for it; a helper's report is at most 16 lines; and a brief points at a note in the repository instead of repeating it. The app shortens the conversation by itself only near 900 thousand tokens, far too late. THE LEAD HANDS OVER AT 300 THOUSAND (measured again at 08:08 UTC on 2026-11-22: at 650 thousand the lead made 124 calls in an hour and cost more than all its helpers together). How: `get_session` on itself says how long the conversation is (`context_usage.used_tokens`); past 300 thousand, at the next moment when no helper of its own is running, it brings `STATUS.md` up to date (a "Handover" part: what is in flight, what to wait for, the next actions in order), pushes, and starts its successor with `create_session` (the strongest model, this repository at the build branch, `outcome_branch` the build branch, a short prompt that says: you are the lead, read `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/build/START-HERE.md`, `docs/build/STATUS.md` and `docs/build/USAGE.md`, you are NOT a session the founder started, so the staging keys and releases are not yours); then it stops working and tells the founder's window. The first lead's session (the chat the founder writes in) stays the founder's window: a lead sends it a message of at most six lines at a milestone, at the day's end, and when something needs the founder; it sends the founder's words on to the lead.
14. **What a week buys (measured on 2026-11-22, so nobody has to guess again).** In two hours of three lanes at once the build used 6% of the week: about 3 points an hour, two thirds of it helpers and one third the lead. That morning landed 8 steps that were already built and took 4 more through building, review and fixing. A step built from nothing costs between half a point and one and a half points of the week with its review, its fixes and the lead's share; a lane that only needs its fix round and landing costs a quarter of a point. So one week pays for roughly 60 to 90 steps' worth of work if nothing is wasted, and NOT for three lanes running day and night (that is 70 points a day). The plan had 127 steps open on 2026-11-22: about two weeks, in the order of `STATUS.md`, "Next step".
